title: Knock an empty open-ended cardboard box down flat for recycling, pressing it over rather than pushing it along
instruction: Flatten the empty cardboard box for recycling, so that it lies flat on the table, and let go of it.
context: Breaking down delivery boxes for the recycling bin is a weekly chore in most homes and a constant one behind every shop counter. An empty box with both ends open is a four-panel tube that folds flat along its corner creases, but it is light and its creases hold it square. Pushed level at its side it slides across the table instead of folding; pressed only part way it springs back up. It folds only under a push that is steep enough, down as well as over, to hold it to the table while it shears, and only stays flat once pressed all the way down so its creases set. The task tests choosing and keeping that force direction as the box's top edge travels along an arc, and finishing the fold, not handling flaps: every flap is already open, unlike tasks that fold a box's flaps closed.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Layout A is given first, layout B in brackets. Box: an empty single-wall regular slotted carton, 20 x 15 x 15 cm inside (length x width x height), brown B-flute corrugated board 3 mm thick, 116 g in all, with all eight flaps (7.5 cm deep) folded out in line with their panels, so it is an open tube 30 cm long including the flaps. It lies on one of its 20 cm panels with the tube running left to right: the 15 cm walls stand up, one facing the arms and one away, and the top panel is 15.3 cm above the table. The crease along the bottom of the wall facing the arms runs at x 21.5 [B: 23.5], and the middle of the tube is at y 0.0 [B: 3.0]; the box spans x 21.4 to 41.7 [B: 23.4 to 43.7] and y -15 to 15 [B: -12 to 18]. Each corner crease resists folding like a spring of 0.12 N m/rad (0.19 N m at 90 degrees). Nothing else is on the table. Both arms start in the raised ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: Tools: a ruler, a protractor or angle app, and the trial video. Read at the end of the run. 1.0 if the box lies flat: its cross-section is sheared at least 80 degrees from square (each wall within 10 degrees of lying flat, either way), no part of it is more than 2.5 cm above the table, its lowest point is within 1 cm of the table top (it is on the table), it is still (every panel moving slower than 5 cm/s), and it is let go (no gripper's grasp point lower than 6 cm above the table over the box's outline grown by 3 cm). Else 0. A box standing square, half folded, folded but held, knocked off the table, or still springing back scores 0.
reset_notes: Open the box back into a square tube along its four corner creases, flaps folded out in line with their panels, and lay it on the same 20 cm panel at the layout's position. A real box's creases soften with each flattening: replace the box when it no longer stands square by itself.
fidelity: Panels are rigid 3 mm boards on four hinged creases with springs; real board bows and its creases are uneven. Flaps are in line with their panels and do not bend at their own creases. The creases' giving way once fully flat is modelled as their springs switching off at 84 degrees of shear. Board-on-table friction is 0.45 static, 0.38 sliding (assumed). Self-contact between panels is replaced by hinge limits at 88 degrees. Grip force is not judged.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both grippers went to the ends of the box several times; it was never pressed and stayed standing square); demo: 1.0 (flat at step 213)
